messages:
Maya S.: Heads-up — we just got a DSAR delete for acct_9921 but the requestor says data was processed under an ephemeral keystore last month. wondering if rotation impacted our ability to produce a deletion proof :thinking:
Ethan P.: Do we have an audit event for the delete op reaching the embedding service? I can’t find a matching `delete_request` log for acct_9921 in the trace IDs provided
Priya R.: Maya — which keystore mode was the tenant on? ephemeral vs customer-managed matters for rewrap. If it was ephemeral we might not be able to decrypt older snapshots after rotation
Maya S.: It was flagged in the portal as `ephemeral-tenant:true` and the keystore TTL was 30d. The DSAR timestamp is within 20d so should be fine but the backend says some snapshots were reencrypted with a new ephemeral key on 2026-02-18
Jordan K.: OpsBot just emitted a warning on 2026-02-18 about a forced rewrap: OpsBot: `keystore:forced_rewrap tenant=acct_9921 reason=rotational_sla_violation`
Maya S.: ok that’s the event. the problem: our erasure pipeline uses the current keystore to produce deletion receipts — if the key rotated and older snapshots are unreadable we might not be able to show deterministic evidence
Anya (Legal): From a compliance POV we need to demonstrate chain-of-custody and either complete deletion or an approved retention exception. If we can’t decrypt evidence, we still must document steps taken and escalate for legal approval
Ethan P.: Quick technical question — do we still have raw object copies in cold snapshots that were never rewrapped? path looks like `s3://redwood-embeds/snapshots/acct_9921/*.enc`
Priya R.: There are two classes: - hot cache (KV store) — rewrapped; - cold snapshots — some were migrated and rewrapped, some left encrypted under old ephemeral key. The KMS history shows old key material has been rotated and destroyed per ephemeral policy
Jordan K.: If key material was destroyed then we cannot produce plaintext proofs. We should mark this a potential retention exception and start the exception workflow
Maya S.: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Freeze deletion attempt for this DSAR and mark incident (inc-privacy-keystore-1819) 2) Collect all metadata: keystore events, OpsBot logs, snapshot object list, policy IDs 3) Legal to advise on retention-exception vs acceptable evidentiary substitution 4) If needed, offer requester redacted/aggregated proof instead of raw plaintext
Anya (Legal): Agree. Also need to check whether requester provided additional identity proof; if they did, we can offer a certified statement of deletion attempts and retention exception justification. I'll draft the statement once we have the logs
Ethan P.: I can assemble a minimal audit bundle. Quick script I’ll run: ```bash
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-embeds/snapshots/acct_9921/ --recursive > /tmp/acct_9921_list
jq '.events | map(select(.tenant=="acct_9921"))' /var/log/keystore/history.log > /tmp/keystore_events.json
```
Priya R.: Also capture KMS key rotation metadata: `gcp-kms history --key=projects/.../keys/ephemeral-acct_9921` — save the `destroy` and `rewrap` entries
Jordan K.: I’ll open the retention-exception ticket in the tracker and link the audit bundle. Ticket created: PRV-4438. tagging @security-oncall
Maya S.: tagging @Ethan P., @Priya R. — can you two own the audit bundle by EOD? I’ll coordinate with Anya for the legal text
Ethan P.: On it. ETA 5pm PT. I’ll paste the bundle link here when done
Priya R.: I’ll export keystore and snapshot manifests and put them in GCS under `gs://redwood-privacy/audit-bundles/PRV-4438/` by 4pm PT
Anya (Legal): Once I review the bundle I’ll advise on whether to accept a retention exception. If yes, I’ll prepare the standard retention-exception letter and include our remediation plan
Jordan K.: Note for the runbook: add a check that ephemeral tenants have a pre-rotation snapshot policy that guarantees retrievability for DSAR window. Filing a follow-up: PRV-4439 to update runbook
Maya S.: Thanks. If we end up unable to decrypt, make sure the bundle includes the OpsBot rewrap event and proof of destruction — that will be critical for legal
OpsBot: incident PRV-4438 created, assigned to security-oncall, severity=medium
Ethan P.: Bundle uploaded: https://storage.redwood/privacy/PRV-4438/audit-bundle.tar.gz — contains snapshot manifest, keystore history, OpsBot logs, and retention policy dump
Maya S.: received. Anya, ping me when you have guidance and I’ll notify the requester with our temporary suspension of deletion while we finalize the exception determination :white_check_mark:
Anya (Legal): Will do. If we deny the exception we need an expedited remediation plan to reconstruct or compensate for data loss. If we approve, we must record the business rationale and approvals
Maya S.: closing loop: next steps documented in PRV-4438. owners: Ethan (audit bundle), Priya (keystore snapshots), Anya (legal). I’ll add a short postmortem checklist after we close
